claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on existing thermodynamic data can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed training data will include free energies and entropy terms.
The model will capture complex relationships between thermodynamic properties and material composition.
Learning patterns from existing data will allow the model to predict thermodynamic properties without costly molecular-dynamics simulations.
The machine-learning predictions will be fast and accurate.
The method will reduce computational cost by at least 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will increase throughput by 20% relative to TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The method will maintain at least 90% fidelity relative to explicit ab initio results.
The proposed method is expected to apply to systems containing up to five components.
The proposed method is expected to apply from 500 K to 2000 K.
The proposed method is expected to apply at pressures from 1 atm to 10 atm.
Model accuracy may be limited by the quality and quantity of the training data.
The model may fail to capture some complex interactions in high-entropy systems.
The model can be benchmarked against explicit ab initio calculations using errors in predicted free energies and entropy terms.
